chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who fights for his wealth. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The one who is killed for his wealth, he is at the status of the martyr.' I said, 'Is his fighting better, or not fighting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, if it were me, I would not fight and leave him.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الشَّهِيدِ: at the status of the martyr

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred action for a Muslim when attacked for their wealth: fight to defend it or leave it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the legal status of martyrdom (*shahada*) and the ethical virtue of *fada'ila* (excellence); while defending wealth grants the rank of a martyr, it is spiritually superior to remain patient and surrender one's possessions rather than engage in combat. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing legal rulings with moral prudence, where the preservation of life and soul often takes precedence over material preservation, even if the latter carries a high spiritual reward.
